headline: Analytic choices and input quality shape single-cell and spatial transcriptomics outputs
label: Single Cell Computational Methods
summary: Failure modes in single-cell and spatial transcriptomics pipelines are now quantified alongside corrective and reproducibility-oriented methods.
synthesis: The dominant thread is scrutiny of analytic choices and input quality in single-cell and spatial transcriptomics pipelines. Random seed choice alters Seurat and Scanpy clustering across 28 datasets, and SABER reassignment is proposed to stabilize it. A benchmark of 20 cell type annotation methods on four expert-labeled spatial datasets assesses accuracy and structure-aware fidelity. Incomplete reference signature matrices degrade cellular deconvolution, which DICEPro addresses, while transcript leakage across platforms, species, and tissues is corrected by the reference-free Bayesian method DeLeakage. Other items extend these concerns toward reference-informed spatial domain detection, GRN-informed subtyping, cell cycle mixture modeling, and differential distribution testing, though their scope varies. The shared feature is pairing quantified failure modes with corrective or reproducibility-oriented solutions.
